title: The Great Bicycle Race
summary: Two neighborhood friends organize a friendly bicycle race around their block, and when one friend's chain breaks mid-race, the other stops to help fix it instead of finishing first alone.
poll: Helping a friend matters more than winning a race.

versions.title: The Great Bicycle Race
versions.text:
Sam and Nour live next door. They both have bikes. They ride every day. They are good friends.

One day, they plan a race. They will race around the block. Sam feels excited. Nour feels excited too.

On race day, they line up. Sam's mom says go. Sam and Nour pedal fast. They ride side by side.

Then Nour hears a loud noise. Clank! The bike chain breaks. Nour stops the bike. Nour looks sad.

Sam is still riding fast. Sam could win the race. But Sam looks back at Nour.

Sam stops the bike too. Sam rides back to Nour. "I will help you," Sam says.

Sam gets off the bike. Sam helps fix the chain. It takes a few minutes. Then the chain works again.

Now they can ride on. But they do not race anymore. They ride to the end side by side.

Nour says thank you. Sam smiles at Nour. A race is more fun with a friend. Helping a friend felt better than a win.

versions.title: The Great Bicycle Race
versions.text:
Sam and Nour are friends. They live right next door to each other. They both have bikes. They love to ride around the block. One day, they decide to have a friendly race.

On the day of the race, Sam and Nour line up at the start. Sam's mom calls out, "Ready, set, go!" Both riders pedal hard. They race side by side down the street.

Partway around the block, Nour hears a loud clank. The bike chain has broken! Nour has to stop pedaling right away. Nour looks down at the bike and feels upset.

Sam is still riding fast. Sam could easily win the race alone. But Sam looks back. Sam sees Nour stopped at the side of the road.

Sam turns the bike around. Sam rides back to where Nour is standing. "Let me help you fix that," Sam says kindly.

Together, they work on the broken chain. It takes a few minutes of careful work. Finally, the chain clicks back into place. It works again.

Now both bikes can move again. But the two friends do not race anymore. Instead, they ride the rest of the way around the block together, side by side.

Nour thanks Sam for stopping to help. Sam just smiles. A race is much more fun with a friend. Helping a friend felt even better than winning alone.

On the morning of the race, Sam and Nour line up their bikes. Sam's mom stands nearby. She calls out, "Ready, set, go!" Both riders push off together. They pedal hard, racing side by side down the street.

Partway around the block, Nour hears a loud, sharp clank from the bike. The bike chain has snapped and broken! Nour has to stop pedaling right away. Nour looks down at the broken chain. Nour feels disappointed and upset.

Meanwhile, Sam is still riding at a good speed. Sam could easily finish the race and win all alone. However, Sam glances back. Sam notices that Nour has stopped at the side of the road.

Without thinking twice, Sam turns the bike around. Sam rides back toward the friend. "Let me help you fix that chain," Sam says kindly.

Together, the two friends work on the broken chain. It takes a few minutes. The chain clicks firmly back into place. It starts working again.

Now both bikes can move once more. But Sam and Nour decide not to race anymore. Instead, they ride the rest of the way together, side by side.

Nour thanks Sam warmly for stopping to help fix the bike. Sam simply smiles. A race always feels more fun when you share it with a good friend. Helping a friend, Sam realizes, felt even better than winning the race alone.

Together, the two friends crouch down and work carefully on the stubborn chain for several long minutes. After some patient effort and a bit of trial and error, the chain clicks firmly back into place. It begins working properly again.

Nour thanks Sam warmly for choosing to stop and help instead of simply riding on ahead to claim an easy victory. Sam just smiles. A race always feels more fun and meaningful when you share it with a true friend. Helping a friend, Sam realizes, felt even better than winning the race entirely alone.

versions.title: The Great Bicycle Race
versions.text:
Sam and Nour are friends who have lived next door to each other for as long as either can remember, sharing the same quiet street their whole lives. They both own bikes, and almost every afternoon they ride together around their block purely for enjoyment. One sunny weekend, the two friends decide it would be exciting to organize a friendly race around the entire block, just to settle who is faster.

On the morning of the race, Sam and Nour carefully line up their bikes at the starting point near Sam's house while curious neighbors watch from their porches. Sam's mother calls out cheerfully, "Ready, set, go!" and both riders push off simultaneously, pedaling hard and racing side by side down the quiet street.

Partway around the block, Nour suddenly hears a loud, sharp clank from somewhere deep inside the bike, and the chain snaps completely in two. Forced to stop pedaling immediately, Nour rolls to a gradual halt near the curb and looks down at the broken chain hanging loosely, feeling both disappointed and a little embarrassed in front of a good friend.

Meanwhile, Sam continues riding at a strong, steady pace, quickly realizing that winning the race alone would now be easy, without any further effort. However, when Sam glances back over one shoulder, Sam notices that Nour has stopped entirely at the side of the road, visibly frustrated and uncertain what to do next.

Without hesitating for even a moment, Sam makes a deliberate decision to turn the bike around, pedaling back toward the friend instead of continuing toward the finish line that still awaits ahead. "Let me help you fix that broken chain," Sam says kindly, already dismounting to kneel beside Nour on the pavement.

Together, the two friends crouch down and work patiently on the stubborn chain for several long minutes, getting a bit of grease on their fingers in the process. Eventually, through persistent effort and some careful trial and error, the chain clicks firmly back into place and begins functioning properly once again.

Now that both bikes can move freely once more, Sam and Nour decide against resuming their competition entirely. Instead, they ride the remaining distance around the block calmly together, pedaling side by side the whole way home without the slightest sense of urgency.

Nour thanks Sam warmly for choosing to stop and assist rather than simply riding ahead to claim an effortless victory. Sam merely smiles and explains that a race always feels more meaningful when shared with a genuine friend. Helping a friend, Sam quietly realizes, felt considerably more rewarding than winning the race entirely alone.

HIGH.prompt: Do you agree that genuine friendship can matter more than winning a competition? Support your position with evidence from the article about Sam and Nour's experience.

HIGH.modelAnswer: I agree that genuine friendship can matter more than winning a competition. Sam's experience in the article shows this clearly: Sam made a deliberate decision to turn back and help Nour fix a stubborn, broken chain, even though continuing on would have guaranteed an easy, uncontested victory. Someone might argue that competitions exist specifically to be won, and that Sam gave up a fair chance at success. However, by choosing not to resume the race afterward and instead riding home together calmly, Sam and Nour show that a genuine friendship, strengthened through helping one another, can feel far more rewarding than any single victory.
